title: The Hammock That Tightened — Pediatric Household Hammock Neck Entanglement, Hypoxic Encephalopathy Despite Normal Head CT & Safe Play-Surface Supervision

teenKit.tldr: An ordinary household hammock fashioned from a soft fabric twisted and unexpectedly trapped a 10-year-old girl's neck, causing a severe oxygen-deprivation emergency. This case proves that everyday soft materials can be just as dangerous as sharp hazards because flexibility allows them to wrap and tighten intensely.
teenKit.whyItMatters: It shatters our dangerous comfort bias, proving that domestic items we trust completely can harbor hidden lethal physics.
keyTakeaways: Softness does not equal safety; flexible fabrics can twist, conform, and constrict the human neck with extreme mechanical pressure.
A normal head CT scan does not automatically mean a brain is safe from severe injury after an oxygen-starvation event.
Forensic case studies strip away assumptions to reveal the exact clinical realities of how household hazards actually operate.
